item.title: Anthropic agrees to $30B round at $900B valuation
item.description:
Anthropic has agreed to terms for a $30 billion fundraising round that would value the AI company at approximately $900 billion, according to a report by the Financial Times on Friday, nearly tripling the startup's valuation from just three months ago.

The round is being co-led by Dragoneer Investment Group, Greenoaks Capital, Sequoia Capital, and Altimeter Capital, each committing $2 billion or more. The deal is expected to close as soon as the end of this month, though final terms could still shift before a formal announcement.

item.title: US and Iran defer uranium talks, prioritize Hormuz
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi confirmed on Friday that Iran and the United States have agreed to defer negotiations over Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile to a subsequent phase of talks, with both sides instead prioritizing the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.

The announcement, reported by Bloomberg on May 15, underscores the persistent deadlock over one of the most contentious issues in the more than two-month-old conflict: the fate of Iran's estimated 400-plus kilograms of uranium enriched to 60% purity, believed to be buried beneath nuclear facilities struck by American bombers last year.

item.title: Iran seizes floating armory near Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Iranian forces boarded and seized a vessel operating as a floating armory in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, diverting it toward Iranian territorial waters in a move that adds a new layer of tension to an already volatile maritime corridor.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), a British military-linked maritime monitoring agency, reported that the vessel was boarded and "taken by unauthorized personnel" while anchored about 38 nautical miles northeast of Fujairah, a key oil export terminal in the United Arab Emirates. Maritime security consultancy Vanguard Tech subsequently identified the ship as the Honduras-flagged Hui Chuan, a fishing support vessel that had been operating as a floating armory — a ship used to store weapons for private security companies that protect commercial vessels from pirate attacks.

item.title: China declines Nvidia H200 chips despite US clearance, Trump says
item.description:
Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One as he returned from a state visit to Beijing, President Donald Trump said on Thursday that China has so far declined to purchase Nvidia H200 artificial intelligence chips, even though Washington has approved their sale. Trump said the issue "did come up" during his meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping but that Beijing "chose not to" buy the chips because it "wants to try and develop their own" domestic alternatives.

The remarks came a day after Reuters reported that the U.S. Commerce Department had cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies — including Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com — to purchase H200 chips, with distributors Lenovo and Foxconn also approved to handle sales. Under the licensing terms, each approved customer may buy up to 75,000 chips, either directly from Nvidia or through authorized intermediaries. Yet not a single delivery has taken place.

item.title: CENTCOM says 72 ships redirected in Iran blockade
item.description:
U.S. Central Command confirmed on Friday that American naval forces have redirected 72 commercial vessels and disabled four ships since the start of a maritime blockade targeting Iranian ports around the Strait of Hormuz, as escalating confrontations at sea continued to rattle global energy markets and shipping lanes.

The update came on a volatile day that also saw a vessel seized near the United Arab Emirates and diverted toward Iranian waters, while an Indian-flagged cargo ship, the MSV Haji Ali, sank off the coast of Oman after a suspected drone or missile strike.

item.title: All 46 Council of Europe nations adopt migration declaration
item.description:
All 46 Council of Europe member states adopted a political declaration on migration on Friday at a meeting in Chișinău, Moldova, setting out a new interpretation of the European Convention on Human Rights that could make it easier to deport certain migrants — including to third-country "return hubs."

The non-binding declaration, the first of its kind on migration from the Council of Europe, was adopted by foreign ministers at the 135th session of the Committee of Ministers. It reaffirms that states have what it calls an "undeniable sovereign right to control the entry and residence of foreign nationals" and that nations facing mass arrivals may pursue new approaches to deter irregular migration.

item.title: Trump calls Takaichi from Air Force One after China summit
item.description:
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and President Donald Trump reaffirmed an "unwavering" bilateral alliance in a phone call on Thursday evening, according to a readout from the Japanese Prime Minister's Office, as Trump flew home from a three-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.

Trump called Takaichi from aboard Air Force One, The Japan Times reported, providing her with a "detailed explanation" of his talks with Xi. The 15-minute conversation covered China-related economic and security affairs, the war in Iran, and cooperation in the Indo-Pacific region. Both leaders agreed to continue close communication and to coordinate ahead of next month's Group of Seven summit in France.

item.title: Trump says US, Nigerian forces killed ISIS's global second-in-command
item.description:
President Donald Trump announced late Friday that U.S. and Nigerian forces had jointly killed Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, whom he described as the global second-in-command of ISIS, in a military operation in Nigeria.

"Tonight, at my direction, brave American forces and the Armed Forces of Nigeria flawlessly executed a meticulously planned and very complex mission to eliminate the most active terrorist in the world from the battlefield," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "He will no longer terrorize the people of Africa, or help plan operations to target Americans."

item.title: Iranian drone strike sparks fire at UAE's Barakah nuclear plant
item.description: A drone strike attributed to Iran caused a fire at an electrical generator on the outer perimeter of the Barakah Nuclear Power Plant in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra region on Sunday, according to Abu Dhabi authorities and reports from Al Jazeera and Gulf News. No injuries were reported, and officials said radiological safety at the facility was not compromised.

item.title: WHO declares Congo-Uganda Ebola outbreak a global health emergency
item.description:
The World Health Organization on Sunday declared the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda a public health emergency of international concern, its highest level of alarm, after more than 300 suspected cases and 88 deaths were reported across the two countries.

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus made the declaration after consulting with both governments, warning of "significant uncertainties to the true number of infected persons and geographic spread" of the disease. The agency said the outbreak is "potentially much larger than what is currently being detected and reported, with significant local and regional risk of spread".

item.title: Trump warns Iran 'the clock is ticking' as strike preparations intensify
item.description:
President Donald Trump escalated his rhetoric toward Iran on Sunday, posting warnings on Truth Social that "the Clock is Ticking" and threatening that there "won't be anything left" of Iran if it does not agree to American terms, as the United States and Israel advanced preparations for a potential resumption of military strikes and a drone attack struck near a nuclear power plant in the United Arab Emirates.

The warnings came as Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a phone call on Sunday. Netanyahu said earlier in the day, "Our eyes are also open regarding Iran. I will speak today, as I do every few days, with our friend President Trump. There are certainly many possibilities, and we are prepared for every scenario."

item.title: Taiwan's Lai vows island 'will not be sacrificed' after Trump-Xi summit
item.description:
Taiwan President Lai Ching-te on Sunday pushed back against the suggestion that the island's security could be used as leverage in U.S.-China diplomacy, declaring that "Taiwan will absolutely not be sacrificed or traded" and that its people will not surrender their democratic way of life under pressure.

Writing on Facebook in his first direct response to last week's summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing, Lai reaffirmed that U.S. arms sales to Taiwan are rooted in the Taiwan Relations Act, the 1979 law that mandates weapons sales to the island, and called them "the most important deterrent force over the years against actions that undermine regional peace and stability".

item.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts three drones from Iraqi airspace
item.description:
Saudi Arabia said on Sunday that its air defenses intercepted and destroyed three drones after they entered the kingdom's territory from Iraqi airspace, marking the latest in a series of aerial threats that have tested Gulf security since the broader Iran conflict erupted earlier this year.

Defense Ministry spokesman Major General Turki Al-Maliki said the kingdom "would take the necessary operational measures to respond to any attempt to violate its sovereignty and security" and vowed to ensure the safety of citizens and residents on Saudi territory, according to Arab News.

item.title: Pakistan shares revised Iran peace proposal with US amid stalled talks
item.description:
Pakistan shared a revised Iranian proposal with the United States on Sunday night aimed at ending the conflict in the Middle East, a Pakistani source told Reuters on Monday, even as peace talks appeared to remain stalled.

"We don't have much time," the source said when asked whether it would take time to close gaps between the two sides, adding that both countries "keep changing their goalposts".

item.title: U.S. offers temporary Iran oil sanctions waiver in new draft text
item.description: The United States has offered to temporarily waive sanctions on Iranian oil exports during active negotiations, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency, marking a potential shift in Washington's approach to ending the nearly three-month war. But the proposal has done little to break the diplomatic deadlock, with Iran demanding full and permanent sanctions removal and President Trump warning Tehran on Sunday that "the clock is ticking."

item.title: Iran launches Strait of Hormuz transit authority as US reinsurance program draws zero takers
item.description: The Trump administration's flagship effort to restart commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a $40 billion government-backed reinsurance program — has failed to attract a single customer, according to industry reports and insurer statements, even as Iran moves to assert sovereign control over the waterway with its own transit authority and a cryptocurrency-backed insurance scheme.

item.title: Pakistan sends 8,000 troops, jets to Saudi Arabia
item.description: Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops, a squadron of around 16 JF-17 fighter jets, two drone squadrons, and a Chinese-made HQ-9 air defense system to Saudi Arabia under a confidential mutual defense agreement, Reuters exclusively reported on Sunday. The deployment, described by five sources as a "combat-capable force," marks the largest Pakistani military commitment to the Gulf kingdom since the 1991 war against Iraq and comes even as Islamabad serves as the principal mediator in the ongoing Iran war.

item.title: Jury sides with OpenAI, rejects Musk's lawsuit
item.description: A federal jury in Oakland, California, sided with OpenAI and Sam Altman on Monday, rejecting Elon Musk's lawsuit alleging the artificial intelligence company betrayed its nonprofit mission when it shifted toward a for-profit model. The nine-member jury found that Musk's case was filed too late, ending the closely watched legal battle that had threatened to upend one of the most valuable private companies in the world.

item.title: Mexico, Uruguay aid ship docks in Havana amid Cuba crisis
item.description: A vessel carrying humanitarian aid from the governments of Mexico and Uruguay docked in Havana on Monday, offering a measure of relief to a nation gripped by its worst energy crisis in decades. The ship, named the Asian Katra, arrived in Havana Bay loaded with food supplies and personal hygiene products as Cuba endures blackouts lasting more than 20 hours a day in parts of the capital.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau helped secure visa for fugitive Polish minister
item.description:
U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau personally directed senior officials to facilitate a visa for Zbigniew Ziobro, a fugitive former Polish justice minister facing 26 criminal charges, enabling him to flee Hungary for the United States, according to a Reuters exclusive report citing three people familiar with the matter.

Landau instructed officials from the State Department's Consular Affairs Bureau to order the U.S. embassy in Budapest to issue the visa, describing the matter as "a national security issue," one source told Reuters. One source described the document as a journalist visa, a characterization that aligns with earlier Polish media reports suggesting Ziobro may be working as a correspondent for TV Republika, a right-wing Polish broadcaster. The sources told Reuters they were unaware of any involvement by President Donald Trump, and it remained unclear what role Secretary of State Marco Rubio played.
